title: Governed list
description: A governed list: a closed set of named values that specs, hubs and modules choose from or are held to. Sender: forge-core, where the owner approves it. Transmission: in the contract, and down the chain of command one level at a time, where it may arrive late or after this format has moved on. Receiver: a runner, a hub's decision point or a person, who must be able to tell from the list alone what it is (list), which construction it is (spec_version), that it is the approved one (integrity) and what each value means (entries). A receiver that does not know the spec_version refuses the list and keeps the last one it understood. A list that needs a vocabulary of its own beside its entries is named in this schema with the fields it adds, as data-classes is; no other list carries them. Three lists of the trust root (D-23) hold their entries to a shape given in $defs: certificate-roles to certificateRole, authenticator-models to authenticatorModel and device-attestation-roots to deviceAttestationRoot. They are bound by name in forge_core.fxts.shared.lists, because a new branch of the top-level allOf is a major step that would send every list back for review (FB-301).

spec_version.description: The version of this format the list is written in.

list.description: The list's name; the file is <list>.list.json.

title.description: What the list is, in a few words.

description.description: What the values are for, who chooses from them, and the decision that set the list.

directions.description: data-classes only: the directions a class of data may travel.

deliveries.description: data-classes only: the delivery rules a class may have.

links.description: data-classes only: the links a class may travel.

integrity.description: The FHTS block: the hash of everything else in the list, its state, and who approved it.

id.description: The value as it is written where it is chosen. Dotted for a child of another entry.

entry.description: One value. A list may give its entries more fields; a list named below is held to the shape given for it.

kind.description: How the limit is tested: by the scopes a decision exercises or grants, or by a relation between who grants and who receives.

scopes.description: Scopes the limit covers, <domain>:<object>:<action>, with * for any.

applies.description: interim: only an interim decision is forbidden, and a behavioral contract may permit the act. always: no decision and no contract permits it.

reason.description: Why no later rejection can put the act right.

status.description: A retired limit stays listed so that a record naming it still resolves; its id is never used again.

enforced_by.description: What holds the limit today: tests or checks, by path or id. Empty when nothing does.

id.description: The role, as the anchor's policy and the verifiers name it.

description.description: What a certificate of this role is for.

issued_by.description: The role whose key signs a certificate of this one; its own id for a self-signed certificate root.

identity.description: The form of its SPIFFE id: spiffe://<deployment>, .../hub/<hub>, or .../hub/<hub>/module/<module>.

ca.description: Whether it may sign certificates (basic constraints, critical).

path_length.description: The path length a CA role carries; null for a leaf.

extended_key_usage.description: Exactly these extended key usages; empty means the extension is absent.

curve.description: The curve of the certificate's key.

signs_with.description: The hash this role's key signs with; null for a role that signs nothing.

certificateRole.description: One role of certificate in the trust root's profile (D-23 T-4): written once, read by the issuer and by both verifiers. No role carries name constraints.

id.description: A name for the model; its AAGUID is a field, since an id starts with a letter.

description.description: The model and the firmware the entry covers.

aaguid.description: The model's AAGUID, as its attestation certificate and authenticator data carry it.

attestation_format.description: Only packed attestation with a certificate chain is accepted (D-23 T-9).

roots.description: The maker's attestation roots for the model, in PEM.

intermediates.description: Intermediates between a root and the model's attestation certificates, which OpenSSH does not write.

required_properties.description: What every enrolment of the model must show: backup-eligible clear, user verification, credProtect level 3.

biometric.description: No model with a biometric method is listed: metadata cannot tell whether several people enrol fingerprints.

fido_certificate.description: The FIDO certification number, checked by hand.

fips_certificate.description: The FIPS 140 (CMVP) certificate number, checked by hand; null when it has none.

source.description: Where each fact came from: the maker's published roots, never FIDO's metadata, which is not redistributed.

authenticatorModel.description: One model of security key a person may enrol (D-23 T-9).

id.description: A name for the attestation root.

kind.description: The kind of device whose key attestation chains to it.

roots.description: The maker's attestation roots, in PEM.

intermediates.description: Intermediates between a root and a device's attestation key.

deviceAttestationRoot.description: One attestation root for the devices that hold the trust root's keys (D-23 T-3).
